question: An L5 nerve root compression characteristically causes sensory loss along the lateral aspect of the lower leg and the dorsum of the foot, with weakness of dorsiflexion of the ankle (foot drop).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. L5 compression causes sensory loss on the lateral leg and foot dorsum plus foot drop (ankle dorsiflexion weakness via tibialis anterior). Confusing L5 with S1 is a common trap — S1 affects the lateral border of the foot and sole, and is associated with loss of the ankle jerk reflex.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. L5 root supplies the lateral leg and dorsum of foot (the web between first and second toes is a reliable L5 sentinel) and innervates tibialis anterior (dorsiflexion) and extensor hallucis longus. This distinguishes L5 from S1 (which gives lateral foot/sole + loss of ankle jerk + plantarflexion weakness).
